measurement.title: What is Measurement?
measurement.intro: Measurement is finding the size, amount, or degree of something using numbers and units.

length.title: Length and Distance
length.intro: Length measures how long something is. Distance measures how far apart two things are.
length.millimeter: Millimeter (mm) - very small, like the thickness of a coin
length.centimeter: Centimeter (cm) - about the width of your pinky finger
length.kilometer: Kilometer (km) - 1000 meters, good for long distances
length.inch: Inch (in) - about the length of your thumb
length.foot: Foot (ft) - 12 inches, about the length of a ruler
length.yard: Yard (yd) - 3 feet, about one big step
length.mile: Mile (mi) - 5,280 feet, used for long distances

weight.title: Weight and Mass
weight.intro: Weight (or mass) measures how heavy something is.
weight.gram: Gram (g) - very light, like a paperclip
weight.kilogram: Kilogram (kg) - 1000 grams, like a bag of sugar
weight.ounce: Ounce (oz) - small weight, like a slice of bread
weight.pound: Pound (lb) - 16 ounces, like a loaf of bread

volume.title: Volume and Capacity
volume.intro: Volume or capacity measures how much space something takes up or how much liquid it can hold.
volume.milliliter: Milliliter (mL) - a few drops of water
volume.liter: Liter (L) - 1000 mL, like a large water bottle
volume.cup: Cup (c) - about 250 mL, a coffee mug

time.title: Time
time.intro: Time measures how long something takes or when something happens.

example1.title: Converting Meters to Centimeters
example1.question: A table is 2 meters long. How many centimeters is that?
example1.step3: Check: 200 cm is bigger than 2 m, which makes sense because centimeters are smaller units

example2.title: Converting Kilograms to Grams
example2.question: A bag of rice weighs 3 kilograms. How many grams is that?

example3.title: Calculating Time
example3.question: A movie starts at 3:00 PM and ends at 5:30 PM. How long is the movie?
example3.answer: The movie is 2 hours and 30 minutes long

exercise1.question: How many inches are in 1 foot?
exercise1.explanation: There are 12 inches in 1 foot. Think of a ruler!

exercise3.question: How many cups are in 1 gallon?
exercise3.explanation: 1 gallon = 4 quarts, 1 quart = 4 cups, so 1 gallon = 4 × 4 = 16 cups

exercise4.question: How many minutes are in 2 hours?

exercise5.question: Which unit would you use to measure the length of your bedroom?
exercise5.explanation: Meters or feet are appropriate for measuring room sizes. Millimeters are too small, kilometers are too large, and grams measure weight, not length!

weightScale.title: Measuring Weight
weightScale.caption: A scale shows how heavy something is
weightScale.label: Kitchen Scale

clock.title: Measuring Time
clock.caption: A clock helps us measure and tell time
clock.label: 3:00 - Hour hand (short, blue), Minute hand (long, green)

notes.tip1: Always include the unit when you write a measurement! 5 meters is very different from 5 centimeters!
notes.trick1: Memory trick for feet: A FOOT has 12 inches, just like a RULER has 12 inches!
notes.warning1: Don't mix up volume and weight! Milliliters (mL) measure liquids, grams (g) measure weight.
notes.tip2: To remember time: There are 60 seconds in a minute and 60 minutes in an hour. Both use 60!

conclusion.title: Great Measuring!
conclusion.summary: You've learned about different types of measurements! These skills help you understand the world around you and solve real problems every day.
conclusion.takeaway1: We measure length (how long), weight (how heavy), volume (how much), and time (how long it takes)
conclusion.takeaway2: Metric system uses meters, grams, and liters; Imperial system uses feet, pounds, and gallons
conclusion.takeaway3: Always include the unit with your measurement (5 cm, not just 5)
conclusion.takeaway4: Converting units: multiply or divide based on the conversion factor (1 m = 100 cm, 1 ft = 12 in)
